# myenergi fixtures

Real answers of the myenergi cloud, taken from the tests of
[CJNE/pymyenergi](https://github.com/CJNE/pymyenergi) (MIT License, © 2020
Johan Isacsson), `tests/fixtures/`:

| File                                                  | From                                       | What it is                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `status.json`                                         | `client.json` (`devices`)                  | `/cgi-jstatus-*`: eddi, two zappi, two harvi, libbi |
| `names.json`                                          | `client.json` (`keys`)                     | `/cgi-get-app-key-`: names given in the app         |
| `status-zappi-harvi-battery.json`                     | `client_1p_zappi_harvi_solar_battery.json` | single phase zappi, harvi, solar and AC battery     |
| `zappi.json`, `eddi.json`, `harvi.json`, `libbi.json` | same names                                 | the status of one device                            |

Anonymized: every serial number was replaced by an invented one (zappi
`11000001` and `11000002`, eddi `21000001`, harvi `31000001` and `31000002`,
libbi `41000001`), the hub key by `H12345678`, the server by
`s18.myenergi.net`. Nothing else was changed.

The hourly history (`/cgi-jdayhour-...`) is generated by the fake cloud of
`test/helpers/fakeCloud.js`, in the format of pymyenergi's `jdayhour.json`
(one row per hour, `hr` left out at midnight, energy counters in joules) with
the `h1d`/`h1b` counters pymyenergi sums for a zappi or an eddi.
